beats.intro: Chapter sixty-six. [[sub]]Before solving a quadratic equation, you can tell how many real solutions it has.
beats.disc: Look again at the quadratic formula. [[part]]The part under the radical, b squared minus four a c, is called the discriminant. [[pm]]The plus or minus adds and subtracts its square root. [[pos]]If the discriminant is positive, its square root is a positive number, and the plus and minus give two different solutions. [[zero]]If it's zero, plus zero and minus zero are the same, so there's one solution. [[neg]]If it's negative, its square root isn't a real number: no real solutions.
beats.slide: Watch it on a graph. [[fam]]Here's y equals x squared plus six x plus c. [[c3]]With c equal to three, the discriminant is thirty-six minus twelve, twenty-four: positive. The parabola crosses the x-axis twice. [[up]]Now raise c. The parabola rises, and the discriminant shrinks. [[c9]]At c equals nine, the discriminant is zero, and the parabola just touches the axis: one solution. [[c11]]At c equals eleven, it's negative eight, and the parabola floats above the axis: no real solutions.
beats.ex: Try one with a fraction. [[q]]One half x squared minus eight x plus thirty-two equals zero. [[abc]]a is one half, b is negative eight, c is thirty-two. [[d]]Negative eight squared is sixty-four, and four times one half times thirty-two is also sixty-four. [[zero]]The discriminant is zero, so there's exactly one solution. [[chk]]The formula confirms it: x equals eight over one, or eight.
beats.form: Make sure the equation is in standard form first. [[q]]Negative two x squared plus seven x equals eight. [[move]]Subtract eight: negative two x squared plus seven x minus eight equals zero. [[d]]Now a is negative two, b is seven, c is negative eight. Forty-nine minus sixty-four is negative fifteen. [[none]]Negative, so there are no real solutions.
beats.q2: Quick check. How many real solutions?
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]The discriminant is b squared minus four a c. [[w2]]Positive: two real solutions. Zero: one. Negative: none. [[w3]]On the graph, that's whether the parabola crosses the x-axis twice, touches it once, or misses it. [[w4]]Write the equation in standard form before reading off a, b, and c. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. Find the discriminant, then solve.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter sixty-six, and of unit twelve.
